---
title: "Directed and Weighted Graph"
subtitle: "How arrows and edge weights change graph meaning"
---

A directed graph has edges that point in one direction only. The arrow shows the edge's source and target, so `A → B` is not the same as `B → A`.

### Directed graph example

::: {.static-graph-inline}
<div id="directed-example"></div>
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
dg_nodes = [
    {"id": "A", "label": "A"},
    {"id": "B", "label": "B"},
    {"id": "C", "label": "C"},
]
dg_edges = [
    {"id": "e0", "source": "A", "target": "B", "label": ""},
    {"id": "e1", "source": "B", "target": "C", "label": ""},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "A", "target": "C", "label": ""},
]
ojs_define(dg_nodes = dg_nodes, dg_edges = dg_edges)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| results: hide
import { mountStaticGraphView } from "./js/static-graph-view.js";

mountStaticGraphView(
  document.querySelector("#directed-example"),
  { nodes: dg_nodes, edges: dg_edges },
  {
    width: 380,
    height: 260,
    directed: true,
    caption: "A directed graph: edges only flow in one direction",
  }
);
```

`A → B` is an arrow that means the connection goes from `A` to `B` only. Directed graphs are useful for one-way roads, data flow, and precedence relationships.

## Weighted Graphs

A weighted graph gives each edge a number called a weight. That number can represent distance, cost, strength, or any value that changes how the graph is used.

### Undirected weighted graph

::: {.static-graph-inline}
<div id="weighted-undirected"></div>
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
wu_nodes = [
    {"id": "A", "label": "A"},
    {"id": "B", "label": "B"},
    {"id": "C", "label": "C"},
]
wu_edges = [
    {"id": "e0", "source": "A", "target": "B", "label": "4"},
    {"id": "e1", "source": "B", "target": "C", "label": "2"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "A", "target": "C", "label": "5"},
]
ojs_define(wu_nodes = wu_nodes, wu_edges = wu_edges)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| results: hide
mountStaticGraphView(
  document.querySelector("#weighted-undirected"),
  { nodes: wu_nodes, edges: wu_edges },
  {
    width: 380,
    height: 260,
    directed: false,
    caption: "An undirected weighted graph: each edge has the same weight both ways",
  }
);
```

In this undirected weighted graph, the edge `A — B` has weight `4`, and that value applies in both directions.

### Directed weighted graph

::: {.static-graph-inline}
<div id="weighted-directed"></div>
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
wd_nodes = [
    {"id": "A", "label": "A"},
    {"id": "B", "label": "B"},
    {"id": "C", "label": "C"},
]
wd_edges = [
    {"id": "e0", "source": "A", "target": "B", "label": "3"},
    {"id": "e1", "source": "B", "target": "C", "label": "1"},
    {"id": "e2", "source": "A", "target": "C", "label": "2"},
]
ojs_define(wd_nodes = wd_nodes, wd_edges = wd_edges)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| results: hide
mountStaticGraphView(
  document.querySelector("#weighted-directed"),
  { nodes: wd_nodes, edges: wd_edges },
  {
    width: 380,
    height: 260,
    directed: true,
    caption: "A directed weighted graph: arrows carry numeric weights",
  }
);
```

A directed weighted graph combines both ideas: each edge has a direction and a numeric weight. The edge `A → B` with weight `3` is not the same as `B → A`.
